_lexo: Recorded 13.10.2026 with the author's screencast tool (cards + live terminal + dashboard screenshots + TTS, hard-trimmed under 180 s). This is the exact scenario behind https://youtu.be/MGK67wLra4c; terminal blocks were executed live, nothing was staged. Paths are relative to the repo root.

rreshtat: A personal agent that 'remembers' for you — but what did it keep, from where, and can you take it back?
Example corpus here: the 744 Python PEPs (public domain). The real one is your own notes.
A confident answer with no source costs more than 'I don't know': you act on it.
blloqet.narracioni: I have run a personal AI agent for a year over my own decisions and lessons. The useful part was never the chat — it was the memory. And the fear was always the same: what did it remember, from where, and can I take it back? Here the archive is public — the Python Enhancement Proposals — so you can rebuild every step.

blloqet.narracioni: This is the product. Retrieval runs locally over plain Markdown files under git; only the six closest units reach NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super on Nebius Token Factory, and it must cite them — the id in brackets is a file you can open. Now a trap: PEP 9999 does not exist. Similar PEPs are retrieved, and the agent says I don't know. The numbers at the top are read live from the harness report, never typed in.

komandat: make run-peps Q="Which PEP added assignment expressions?"

ARK_ARKIVA=arkiva-peps python3 src/remember.py --kategoria shenim --id nebius-video-4 --burimi 'screencast 2026-10' --tekst 'Final take: Nemotron 3 Super on Nebius Token Factory answered the PEP questions with citations; PEP 9999 was refused.' --indeks
echo 'make run-peps Q="Which PEP is the style guide?"' | at now + 2 minutes 2>&1 | tail -1
blloqet.narracioni: The same from the command line — and then the agent acts. Remember: it writes a new memory unit and commits it; the git log is the audit trail, and one embedding call updates the index. Audit: for any unit you can ask what, from where, when, who, and how to revert — answered from files and git, not from the model. Remind: it schedules a job on its own scheduler. Every action leaves a commit or a job id, not a promise. The body is an isolated OpenClaw profile with four skills — ask, remember, remind, and web.

imazhet.caption: Memory panel: git log of what the agent remembered — a sha opens the diff, an id opens the unit
Web with permission: archive first, Tavily second — one answer citing [pep-0572] and [w3] side by side

blloqet.narracioni: The memory panel is the git log: what was remembered, when, in which commit — read it, diff it, revert it. And the web, only with your permission: unticked, the privacy gate refuses and nothing leaves the machine. Ticked, Tavily fetches the pages, Nemotron reads your archive first and the web second, and cites both — the archive knew the PEP, the web knew the Python release.

Routing, same sets, same day: Nano 11/13 · Super 12/13 · Ultra 10/13 at 3.3× the cost — Super stays default
$0.0007 per question · p50 about 3 s · 39 tests · the README quotes the report file, and a test fails if they disagree
blloqet.narracioni: The numbers: thirteen of thirteen on the public corpus, all four traps refused; eighty-eight of a hundred on the larger set, every trap refused. Twelve of thirteen on the private corpus — the miss is kept in the README. We measured Nano, Super and Ultra on the same questions the same day: Ultra bought nothing at three times the cost, so Super stays the default. Under a tenth of a cent per question.
